Hard Disk Copy Guide Using Robocopy

Purpose: Copy data from Hard Disk 1 to Hard Disk 2 without overwriting existing files

Data Volume: ~2TB

Recommendation: Use Robocopy (Not C#)

Bottom Line: Use a simple batch file with robocopy command. It's faster, more reliable, and requires zero development time.

Why Robocopy Over C#?

Factor Robocopy C# Application
Performance ✓ Highly optimized for file operations ✗ Slower due to managed code overhead
Development Time ✓ Ready to use immediately ✗ Requires significant development
Features ✓ Built-in resume, retry, multi-threading ✗ Must implement everything from scratch
Reliability ✓ Battle-tested on billions of operations ✗ Prone to bugs with large datasets

Simple Solution - Batch File

The Simplest Possible Script (2 Lines)

robocopy "D:" "E:" /E /XC /XN /XO /MT:16
pause

Step-by-Step Instructions

Step 1: Open Notepad
Step 2: Copy the 2 lines above
Step 3: Change "D:" to your source hard disk drive letter
Step 4: Change "E:" to your destination hard disk drive letter
Step 5: Save as copy.bat (select "All Files" as file type, not .txt)
Step 6: Right-click the .bat file and select "Run as Administrator"
Step 7: Watch the progress in the command window
Example: If source is F: and destination is G:
robocopy "F:" "G:" /E /XC /XN /XO /MT:16
pause

Robocopy Switch Explanations

Switch Description Why We Need It
/E Copy subdirectories (including empty ones) Ensures complete directory structure is copied
/XC eXclude Changed files Skip files that already exist on destination
/XN eXclude Newer files Skip if newer version exists on destination
/XO eXclude Older files Skip if older version exists on destination
/MT:16 Multi-threaded with 16 threads Speeds up copy operation significantly
Combined Effect: The /XC, /XN, and /XO switches together ensure that ONLY files that don't exist on HD2 will be copied from HD1.

Optional Enhancements

Version with Logging and Retry Logic

robocopy "D:" "E:" /E /XC /XN /XO /R:3 /W:5 /MT:16 /LOG:copy_log.txt
pause

Additional switches explained:

  • /R:3 - Retry 3 times on failed copies
  • /W:5 - Wait 5 seconds between retries
  • /LOG:copy_log.txt - Creates a log file of the operation

Performance Expectations

Speed depends on:

  • Drive type (HDD vs SSD)
  • Connection type (USB 2.0/3.0, SATA, etc.)
  • File sizes (many small files vs. few large files)

Robocopy will maximize whatever bandwidth is available on your hardware.

Important Notes

  • Always run as Administrator for full file access permissions
  • The operation can be interrupted and resumed safely
  • Robocopy shows real-time progress during the copy
  • For 2TB of data, expect the operation to take several hours depending on hardware
  • Ensure destination drive has sufficient free space before starting
⚠ Important: Test with a small folder first to verify the command works as expected before running on 2TB of data!
